note: The pin for the RAW EM++ LANE — the fourteen modules that never reach the SDK compiler and drive a repo-local Emscripten directly. Read scripts/lib/emsdk-toolchain.mjs for why this file exists and what it is allowed to decide. Graph task: modules-raw-emcc-lane-unpinned-toolchain.

pin.why: Every build.mjs in this lane already SAID `emsdk install 6.0.1`, and it is the newest of the three Emscriptens measured in the shipped bytes. Making it the pin is therefore the smallest true statement, not a new choice.

em-5.0.6.note: Present on the build machine under analysis/conjunction-assessment/deps/emsdk. Not used by any module in this lane; recorded so the census is complete and a future stray resolution is recognised rather than mistaken for the pin.

em-5.0.5.note: analysis/od/deps/emsdk. Its emsdk COMMIT is unrecoverable: the 137 bootstrap files are tracked INSIDE this repo rather than being a checkout, so it has no .git of its own and `git rev-parse HEAD` there answers with the modules repo's HEAD. The emscripten release hash is the only identity it can still produce.

shippedToolchainEvidence.note: What produced the CURRENTLY COMMITTED bytes of each lane module, established 2026-08-09. `proven` = rebuilt under that toolchain from committed source, with the toolchain-decided sections (type/import/function/table/memory/global/export/elem, and code to within a handful of bytes) matching the committed artifact exactly. It deliberately does NOT require whole-artifact byte-identity: these builds embed an SDK-encoded manifest, so the SDK is a second build input and a stale artifact can differ there while the compiler question is settled. `strong` = the only Emscripten the module's own resolution order could have reached, installed before the artifact's commit and still present on the build machine. `none` = the emsdk that built it no longer exists on any machine we have; unrecoverable, and recorded as such instead of guessed.

PROVEN by reconstruction 2026-08-09: rebuilding committed source under em-6.0.1 emits a wasm whose type, import, function, table, memory, global, export, elem and datacount sections are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed artifact — same 29 types, 6 imports, 112 functions, 9 exports — with the code section differing by 3 bytes in 56,304. A different Emscripten does not land on the same function count and section bytes by accident. The artifact as a whole is NOT byte-identical, and the reason is not the toolchain: see scripts/artifact-provenance.json unreproducibleReasons.

propagator/sgp4.note: Rebuilt 2026-08-10 under the declared pin (SDN_LOCAL_EMSDK_DIR pointed at data-source/iss-source/deps/emsdk) while adding plugin_entity_apply_impulsive_burn, so WHAT produced the committed bytes is now recorded. It is deliberately NOT in laneModules yet: adding it made three of this repo's own lane tests fail, and they were right to. propagator/sgp4 builds from build.SH, not build.mjs; it does not route through scripts/lib/emsdk-toolchain.mjs; and its ensure_emscripten `git clone`s emsdk and `curl`s the SQLite amalgamation when they are absent — exactly the two things the lane forbids, because a build that downloads its own compiler cannot be reproduced from committed source. Claiming the pin before the build obeys it would be a pin that lies. Filed as modules-sgp4-build-bypasses-the-pinned-emsdk-resolver.

vendoredSources.note: Non-toolchain third-party source these builds compile in. Same rule as the toolchain: resolved locally or refused, never fetched at build time.
